questions.question: Who led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt?
questions.explanation: God called Moses from the burning bush to lead the Israelites out of Egypt.

questions.question: Who built the ark to survive the great flood?
questions.explanation: God instructed Noah to build an ark of gopher wood to preserve his family and every kind of animal.

questions.question: In what town was Jesus born?
questions.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, fulfilling Micah's prophecy.

questions.question: Who defeated the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone?
questions.explanation: Young shepherd David trusted in the Lord and struck Down the Philistine giant Goliath.

questions.question: What is the first book of the Bible?
questions.explanation: Genesis means 'Beginning' and opens with 'In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.'

questions.question: Who was swallowed by a great fish when he tried to run from God's call?
questions.explanation: Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish before preaching to Nineveh.

questions.question: Who was thrown into a den of lions for praying to God?
questions.explanation: God sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths so they would not hurt Daniel.

questions.question: How many disciples (apostles) did Jesus choose to walk closely with Him?
questions.explanation: Jesus chose twelve disciples whom He also named apostles.

questions.question: Which psalm begins with 'The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want'?
questions.explanation: King David wrote Psalm 23 reflecting on God's care as a Good Shepherd.

questions.question: What is the last book of the New Testament?
questions.explanation: Revelation (Apocalypse) written by John on Patmos concludes the New Testament.

questions.question: Which king of Israel was renowned above all others for his God-given wisdom?
questions.explanation: When God offered Solomon anything, he asked for an understanding heart to govern God's people.

questions.question: What was the Apostle Paul's Hebrew name before his ministry to the Gentiles?
questions.explanation: Saul of Tarsus encountered the risen Christ on the road to Damascus and became known as Paul.

questions.question: Where did Jesus perform His first recorded miracle of turning water into wine?
questions.explanation: Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding feast in Cana of Galilee.

questions.question: Which woman of Moab stayed loyal to her mother-in-law Naomi and said, 'Your God will be my God'?
questions.explanation: Ruth accompanied Naomi to Bethlehem and became the great-grandmother of King David.

questions.question: How many days and nights did Jesus fast in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights before overcoming the temptations in the wilderness.

questions.question: Who climbed a sycamore tree in Jericho just to see Jesus pass by?
questions.explanation: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, was short in stature and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus.

questions.question: Which prophet challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel?
questions.explanation: God answered Elijah's prayer with fire from heaven on Mount Carmel.

questions.question: According to Galatians 5:22, what is listed first among the fruit of the Spirit?
questions.explanation: 'But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.'

questions.question: Who was the Jewish queen of Persia who risked her life to save her people from Haman's plot?
questions.explanation: Mordecai encouraged Queen Esther that she had come to the royal position 'for such a time as this.'

questions.question: Which Pharisee came to visit Jesus at night to ask about God's Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Jesus explained to Nicodemus what it means to be born again and spoke the words of John 3:16.

questions.question: Who was the oldest man recorded in the Bible, living 969 years?
questions.explanation: Methuselah, son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah, lived 969 years.

questions.question: On which island was the Apostle Paul shipwrecked on his voyage to Rome?
questions.explanation: After the shipwreck, Paul and all 276 people aboard safely reached the island of Malta (Melita).

questions.question: Who was the female judge and prophetess who led Israel alongside Barak?
questions.explanation: Deborah held court under the Palm of Deborah and accompanied Barak to Mount Tabor.

questions.question: What was the name of the Babylonian king who saw the handwriting on the wall?
questions.explanation: Daniel interpreted the inscription 'MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN' for King Belshazzar.

questions.question: Which short New Testament letter was written by Paul to a Christian slave owner on behalf of Onesimus?
questions.explanation: Paul appealed to Philemon to welcome Onesimus back no longer as a bondservant, but as a beloved brother.

questions.question: Who was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles?
questions.explanation: The lot fell on Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book never explicitly mentions the name of God, yet shows His providence throughout?
questions.explanation: The Book of Esther does not contain the explicit name of God, though His deliverance of Israel is central to the narrative.

questions.question: Who was the high priest's servant whose right ear Peter cut off and Jesus healed in Gethsemane?
questions.explanation: John identifies the servant's name as Malchus, and Luke records that Jesus touched his ear and healed him.

questions.question: Which king of Judah had 15 years added to his life after praying to the Lord during a fatal illness?
questions.explanation: God heard Hezekiah's prayer, saw his tears, and sent Isaiah back to tell him 15 years would be added to his life.

questions.question: In which city were the disciples first called 'Christians'?
questions.explanation: Barnabas and Saul taught a great multitude in Antioch for a whole year, and the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
